title: Agent scaling bets: child browser subagents and WebMCP page tools (site playbooks and MCP exposure are covered by F-t2-043 and F-t2-064)
summary: Four independent, later-stage bets: URL-pattern-bound site playbooks (guidance only, never permissions) injected into browser observations and learned from successful run receipts; child browser runs with narrower child grants (read-only class, capped concurrency) spawned by a parent run; browser.observe/act exposed as an MCP tool behind the same broker grants and approvals; and WebMCP page-tool discovery executed as sensitive-class actions with one-shot approval.
whyItMatters: Playbooks raise success on common SaaS UIs, subagents give parallel research, MCP exposure lets external agents use Verevon's governed browser, and WebMCP positions Quarry for sites that publish typed tools.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Aside (sixteen SKILL.md playbooks with autoInject {keywords, url}; subagent profiles with isolated browser state) and Codex (CDP WebMCP.enable per frame with toolsAdded/Removed events)
others: Aside outbound-only relay with allowlisted remote operations
Codex CI109 signed browser-access attestation for cloud agents
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Playbooks 2 of 3 (common); remote drivers 2 of 3 (common); subagents 1 of 3 (unique); WebMCP 1 of 3 (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Playbooks: registry keyed by URL pattern or keywords, injected into the next observation header and marked as guidance. Subagents: spawn(profile, task) gives a new session with its own browser binding and a tool set filtered by profile, results returned as text. WebMCP: enable the domain per frame, keep a per-tab tool registry, expose tools as webmcp:<host>:<tool> with per-site permission and review.

verevonToday.gap: Quarry supports parallel runs and any authorised device can drive sessions (cloud-native, no relay needed). No URL-bound skills (grep of Model Plane found none), no WebMCP handling in Quarry crates, and neither child-grant fan-out from execution-core nor MCP exposure of browser tools is evidenced; these were not verified in code.

approach: Model Plane: URL-bound skills injected into observations (seed a few top sites, learn more via procedure compile in browser_procedure.rs); child browser runs with child grants and a per-org concurrency cap; MCP tool wrapper over the same grants. Ingestion Plane: discover WebMCP tools in observations and execute them as sensitive-class actions with fenced descriptions. Schedule each separately.
risks: Stale playbook selectors; cost explosion from subagents (cap concurrency per org); external clients must never obtain grants outside the user's ACL; page-defined tools are untrusted input.

verevon.exactGap: Delegated subagents are shipped in Model Plane (nested agent loop, depth 1, per-run ceiling default 8 and hard cap 100, research fan-out) and the in-loop browser.observe and browser.act aliases exist behind a broker-validated grant, but delegated children are leaf-role and refused browser_agent and browser.act as risky, so there are no child browser runs. Missing: a read-only browser action class in broker grants (grant.go carries allowed actions only for sensitive scopes), any per-org live browser run cap (Quarry has only global lease pools), and any WebMCP handling (no code anywhere; the only mention is an outbound 'expose Verevon actions to in-browser agents' bridge in the root plan Verevon-ai-first-plan.md, the opposite direction to Quarry discovering page tools). External MCP exposure of browser tools is not in the gateway, whose mcp.rs only proxies the MCP-server registry.

verevon.constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes: WebMCP descriptors discovered in a page are untrusted input and must be fenced, and their execution must go through a Quarry action with a fresh one-shot broker approval grant, never directly from the Model Plane. Child grants must be strict subsets of the parent (ParentGrantID shape) and may never widen the owner's ACL or a Space's authority; the leaf-role rule (agent.rs:1628-1665) must be relaxed only for a defined read-only browser class, not generally. The shared Chromium process means parallel child runs share one browser, and today a UI session (1280x800) and a Model Plane run (no viewport) already force relaunches that drop each other's pages, so that must be fixed before fan-out. ZDR inheritance by child runs was not verified (INF) and must be confirmed before browser children ship.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Follow the title: remove site playbooks (F-t2-043) and the MCP exposure wrapper (F-t2-064; the in-loop browser.observe and browser.act aliases already exist) from the summary and approach. For child browser runs: reuse run_delegated_child, add a read-only browser action class to BrowserBroker grants (F-t2-032) with a leaf-role exception limited to that class, add a per-org live-run cap in Quarry, and first make viewport page-scoped so concurrent runs stop relaunching Chromium. Keep WebMCP as a research spike only (the CDP WebMCP domain is experimental, INF) and do not schedule it until real sites publish tools.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for child browser runs, which are L because they depend on action classes (F-t2-032), a per-org cap and the viewport fix; WebMCP is a separate M spike.
verevon.verdictReason: Partial is accurate: subagents and in-loop browser MCP aliases already exist, so the item should not read as greenfield, and child browser runs are specifically blocked by the leaf-role risky-tool rule and missing action classes. The summary and approach still describe playbooks and MCP exposure that the title assigns elsewhere, and WebMCP should be demoted to a spike.
